properties.description: Derive a Keep a Changelog-shaped draft (keepachangelog.com, Anthony's pointer 2026-07-28) between any two Releases or Epochs, from what the graph already records: the INCLUDES delta between two Release manifests (what appeared, what left) plus the dated ChangeEvents and drift accepts between their epochs, classified into the KaC buckets — Added / Changed / Deprecated / Removed / Fixed — mapped from the vocabulary the graph already carries (new nodes and link_artifact baselines -> Added; design_updated accepts and amended statements -> Changed; retire-from-design with history -> Deprecated/Removed; design_holds accepts with change_type test_failure_fix -> Fixed). The [Unreleased] section is the standing case: everything dated after the last deployed Release — which makes 'what would this increment's changelog say?' answerable BEFORE cutting it, the capability-increment sibling of what-next. Two KaC principles carried over as constraints: changelogs are FOR HUMANS, curated — this emits a DRAFT a person edits, never a commit-log dump (KaC names raw logs an antipattern; dec:report-dont-judge is the same rule here) — and every entry says what a CONSUMER does about it, which the graph cannot know alone. Kin to cap:compare-designs (two as-designed records); this compares two moments of ONE design and renders the difference in the format industry already reads. DIRECTIONALITY, Anthony's formulation 2026-07-28, which is the load-bearing claim: 'our delta is a graph/machine version of a human changelog; the agent could derive the human changelog from the graph delta. Basically: graph delta --via_agent--> human changelog.' The graph delta is the primary, machine-readable record; the human changelog is a derived rendering, and never the other way around -- when the two disagree, the graph is what is interrogated and the changelog is what gets regenerated.
properties.name: A changelog is a derivable view of the graph's own delta
